data.title: Nvidia live updates: Nvidia stock falls as exuberance fades after Jensen Huang's return as CEO
data.summary: Wall Street analysts cheer Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia — but they still have concerns Bernstein analysts were quick to upgrade Nvidia ( NVDA) on Monday after the board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO of the AI chipmaker, though Wall Street sees ongoing investigations as a lingering overhang on the company. The stock surged as much as 32% following Huang's reinstatement. President Trump said he spoke to the board and "convinced" them to reinstate Huang. His first day back is winning most of it back in a way Wall Street hasn't seen since Cisco (CSCO) in 2001. data.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump calls board
data.summary: In a previous social media post, Trump said the federal government had “no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.” Nvidia’s stock soared 31% on the news, buoying the market after a technology sell-off Friday that seemed to confirm anxieties about a bubble in the AI sector. Nvidia’s advanced computer chips power key AI firms’ models, and the company has helped finance the country’s massive investment in new data centers. [...] Jensen Huang will return as Nvidia’s president and CEO, the company’s board announced Monday, in a stunning reversal for an executive who resigned two weeks ago following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy. The move is effective immediately, the chip giant said in a statement. The company said the board’s unanimous decision to reinstate Huang came after “input from senior levels of the United States government.” [...] “I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,” Huang said in his statement. The reinstatement was all the more dramatic given that Nvidia’s newly installed chairman, Harvey Jones, effectively dismissed this possibility last week. “The Nvidia Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said in a statement on Nov. 17.

data.title: NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director | NVIDIA Newsroom
data.summary: NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United [...] “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” [...] The Board also recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The committee is engaging counsel with experience in national security matters, and such counsel will be retaining advisors with expertise in national security matters. data.title: Trump owned millions in Nvidia stock while pushing for Jensen Huang's reinstatement
data.summary: In a first on CBS News, financial disclosures reveal that President Trump owned tens of millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares, giving him a personal interest in the company's success. The president defends his involvement, saying he personally spoke with the board of the company in a push to get Jensen Hong reinstated as CEO, but the records also indicate that Trump stood to lose a lot of money as a result of Hong's departure and stock decline. When it was announced that Hong would be [...] that Hong would be returning, Nvidia's stock surged by more than 30%. Nvidia stock has slid since the stock market closed Monday. It ended the day down nearly 4% today. Officials told CBS News that a driving factor in the president's support of Huang is fear of the impact of a weak Nvidia and what it could have on the larger US economy. data.title: Trump White House faces corruption questions over Nvidia scandal
data.summary: In the immediate aftermath of Huang’s reinstatement, the president got the huge market rally he was clearly looking for. In fact, Monday’s surge in Nvidia’s shares appears to have added millions of dollars to Trump’s personal wealth. According to recent financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics, the president may have owned as many as 370,000 shares in Nvidia as of Sept. 30, meaning he could have made as much as $15 million off Monday’s surge alone. (The White House has [...] The scandal has even put some Republicans at odds with the president. Republican Sen. Tom Cotton of Arkansas posted, “The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it’s not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back.” He added, “Congress has much to investigate and we will pass overwhelmingly bipartisan chip export-control bills.” Republican Sen. Kevin Cramer of North Dakota also weighed in, suggesting that Huang may need to have a “babysitter.” [...] By Tuesday, the sugar high wore off a bit as Nvidia dropped nearly 6%, pulling the S&P and Nasdaq down with it. Some of those immediate gains from Monday were erased because this is not about just one CEO; it’s about whether the record-shattering multitrillion-dollar investment boom in artificial intelligence can be sustained. Trump can make splashy interventions to move markets for a day, but they tend to have diminishing returns as gravity reasserts itself.
